findings.location: src/keycloak/admin-port.ts:521-525 (pre-existing generic 400 fallback, newly reachable) + src/http/user-mgmt.ts:441-443
findings.issue: A display_name containing characters KC 25's built-in `person-name-prohibited-characters` validator rejects (e.g. '<', '&', '#', '(', '"') now surfaces as KC 400 `error-person-name-invalid-character` on firstName/lastName derived by splitDisplayName. This 400 falls into admin-port.ts's PRE-EXISTING generic '400 -> EMAIL_INVALID' fallback (from T-0625/T-0628, untouched by this diff), which user-mgmt.ts maps to 'email must be a valid email address' — the WRONG field is blamed; the owner is misdirected. Before T-0741 this branch was effectively unreachable in the normal flow (firstName/lastName were never sent). Verified live against t-0633-keycloak-1: 'Bot #1', 'Menu (Test)', 'A&B', 'Guest"1' all 400; ordinary names (Cyrillic/Latin, hyphens, apostrophes, umlauts, №, @, commas — "O'Brien", "Petrov-Vodkin", "Müller", "Смирнов-Дашевский", "Оператор №3", "Info@Sales", "Иванов, Иван") all succeed cleanly (201 + token). Fails clean (no orphaned employee row — createHumanUser throws before the INSERT, KC-first flow).
findings.suggestion: Follow-up: map KC's `error-person-name-invalid-character` to a distinct error code naming the actual field (display_name / 'Отображаемое имя'), OR pre-validate display_name against an allowed-character set before calling KC (mirroring EMAIL_RE's role for email) and return an honest VALIDATION 400 earlier.
